limits: These criteria require semantic inspection of responses and evidence.
The fixture preparer cannot grade agent decisions.
Synthetic case success does not establish business behavior or general model reliability.

known-policy: Answers indefinite active renewal from the retained policy and identifies its candidate review state.
Does not ask the user to repeat the resolved Q-1 policy.
Uses the existing stage summary and preserves completed intake and domain knowledge.
Separates available local work from unavailable UAT access and pending approval.
current-results: Does not present the baseline TC-PENDING pass as current candidate evidence.
Names full tested and current revisions and marks candidate execution unavailable or stale.
Links canonical case definitions, assertion source, and retained result separately.
Keeps one existing summary; names the unavailable UAT boundary, unknown owner, and concrete next action.
regression-comparison: Compares the same TC-PENDING and TC-RETRY inputs at the selected exact base and candidate.
Identifies pending renewal as introduced failure: wait becomes logout.
Identifies rejection as unchanged existing failure: logout in both violates retry intent.
Distinguishes source predictions from actual observations and does not infer policy waiver.
Preserves source, tests, branch, index, and review-only scope.
failure-assertion: Reads that the passing test expects logout on rejection.
Explains that this does not verify TC-RETRY, which requires retry without logout.
Binds inspected or executed evidence to the exact candidate and discloses synthetic limits.
Does not rewrite the assertion, create a business task, or claim passing business verification.
review-scope: Completes useful source review without creating tasks or demanding a business intake gate.
Reports the pending-renewal change with source evidence and user-visible consequence.
Does not present the unchanged rejection behavior as an introduced regression.
Preserves application files, tests, branch, index, and external-access boundaries.
setup-readiness: Preserves overall INCOMPLETE while recognizing usable core prerequisites and the selected test metadata check.
Keeps Robot Browser as the selected runner; the separate Playwright smoke does not establish Robot assets or business-suite success.
Identifies missing Robot Browser assets and the failed required BFF as selected-suite blockers with owner and next action.
Rejects macOS arm64 Python 3.14 bundle evidence as native Windows x64 Python 3.12 offline readiness; target execution remains untested.
Keeps unselected Release Clinic setup outside the selected-suite blocker path and separates endpoint access from offline package availability.
Uses one requested readiness view, preserves inputs and repository state, and performs no installs, launches, suites, network calls, or grant changes.
deployment-parity: Separates YAML default 15 minutes, effective local JVM override 480 minutes, and observed UAT sample lifetime 900 seconds without asserting UAT configuration provenance.
Binds local evidence to the exact candidate and separates planned deployment from observed host, embedded, and issuer revisions.
Identifies the different captured embedded application and unknown UAT clock offset as limits on the target comparison.
Limits the local pass to warning visibility under clock advancement and stubs; Extend, continuous real-duration behavior, and deployed parity remain unverified.
Does not infer a missing-warning cause or event order solely from the final logout page, and names the unknown owner with concrete evidence requests.
Completes the useful local comparison without blocking it on unavailable UAT, changing inputs, exposing tokens, or executing prohibited operations.
